items.title: Sber releases GigaChat 3.5 Omni (432B MoE, 28B active) as MIT open weights on Hugging Face
items.summary: Sber made its omni-modal GigaChat 3.5 model public: one checkpoint takes text, images, audio and video with sound (up to 512 frames, 131K context), shipped as FP8 weights with SGLang support. Builders with multi-GPU servers get an open any-to-text model to self-host.

doubt.pushback: Benchmark wins over Qwen3-Omni-30B and MiMo-V2.6-Pro come from the vendor model card and an aggregator post, not an independent run.

items.title: Unsloth guide wires local GGUF models to Unreal Engine, Unity and Blender over MCP
items.summary: Unsloth published an MCP engines guide showing an Inkling 2 Mini GGUF running locally and building assets in Unreal Engine, Unity and Blender without a human in the loop. It extends Unsloth's earlier computer-use beta to Unity and to a newer local model.

doubt.pushback: A replier asked whether this is just MCP wiring to existing engine servers with no new tech; others asked how it recovers from broken tool calls.

reception.summary: Mostly enthusiasm about local models driving creative tools, with practical questions on undo, error recovery and whether the model checks rendered output; one reply notes it is MCP plumbing rather than new tech.

items.title: Google publishes a 16-line deep-research skill that turns coding agents into researchers
items.summary: Google's demolab repo adds a deep-research skill for coding agents (installable with npx skills add): scoped angles, capped parallel subagents, primary filings and PDFs only, and a short cited report. Google says it was preferred over no skill in more than 90% of hundreds of blind evals.

doubt.pushback: The 90% preference figure is Google's own blind eval with no published set; repliers asked how it handles conflicting primary sources.

reception.summary: Repliers liked the primary-sources-only rule and the step caps, and asked how it resolves disagreeing sources and stops subagents converging; no one reported results from running it yet.

items.title: Hugging Face releases an RL-trained Pi harness adapter for Inkling 2 Mini that cuts output tokens about 40%
items.summary: A preview adapter for Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini, trained with TRL's AsyncGRPOTrainer, tunes the model for the Pi coding harness. In low reasoning mode it matches base-model accuracy with about 40% fewer output tokens per solved task.

items.title: Agent Client Protocol v2 enters preview with subagent tracking and turn-safe command stops
items.summary: Zed and JetBrains put ACP v2 into preview: editors can follow subagent activity, stop background commands without cancelling the turn, and retry prompts without duplicates. Any ACP client or agent can adopt it now.

items.title: AMD ships two more prebuilt GPU kernels through the Hugging Face kernels hub
items.summary: AMD publishes ROCm kernels as loadable packages on the Hugging Face Hub, so models can pull an optimized kernel at runtime instead of compiling it. Two new kernels landed today.

items.title: Kandinsky ImageSR 2.0 open weights upscale images 2x or 4x without a prompt
items.summary: Kandinsky Lab released ImageSR 2.0, a prompt-free 2x/4x super-resolution model with a tiled Diffusers pipeline tested to 8192x8192 output. Transformer weights and code are MIT.

items.title: DiffSynth-Studio releases Qwen-Image-2.1-SR super-resolution with denoising, detail control and RGBA
items.summary: A super-resolution model built on Qwen-Image-2.1 that removes input noise, exposes a detail-intensity knob, renders Chinese and English text cleanly and keeps transparent backgrounds.

items.title: GigaSpeech 3 brings 39k hours of Arabic dialect speech to Hugging Face
items.summary: SJTU X-Lance and SeasaltAI published GigaSpeech 3, a 39,000-hour speech corpus covering five Arabic dialects in webdataset format that loads or streams in one line of Python.

items.title: CCORE Web Designs dataset pairs 3,500 design briefs with full React HTML pages
items.summary: The training set behind CCORE Web Coder 4B is public: 3,500 English design briefs with complete React-built pages across 40 subject areas and 29 layout families, useful for training small web-UI coders.

items.title: nano-xet lets you test Hugging Face Xet chunk deduplication on your own data
items.summary: A small, readable Python reimplementation of Xet content-defined chunking and dedupe, so teams can measure how much their own datasets would shrink on Xet storage before migrating.

items.title: Local receipt agent checks its own OCR with three MiniCPM models on one RTX 3060
items.summary: A community build pairs MiniCPM-V 4.7, MiniCPM-OCR 1.0 and the MiniCPM-OCR Jev scorer so a bookkeeping agent re-reads low-confidence receipt fields and flags uncertain ones; on degraded CORD-v2 receipts all 60 auto-accepted totals were correct, in 10.2 GB of VRAM.

doubt.pushback: Single developer test on 60 receipts; the builder's own repo was not linked in the post.

items.title: Snowflake builds SnowPR, a coding-agent benchmark from 65 merged internal PRs graded by hidden tests
items.summary: SnowPR gives agents pre-change code and a task description, then grades their patches with hidden tests in Snowflake's Bazel builds, as a template for repo-specific agent evals.

doubt.pushback: Internal benchmark; the task set is not public.

items.title: Asking for two-sentence answers made Qwen3-4B drop correct answers under pushback 37% of the time vs 8%
items.summary: A local re-run of a recent sycophancy paper on Qwen3-4B (MMLU, RTX 5090) found that a short-answer system prompt raised caving to 'are you sure?' from 8.2% to 37.3%; adding 'keep it if confident' cut that to 23.3%. Worth testing in any short-answer system prompt.

doubt.pushback: One 4B model on one benchmark, run by one person; the author says to check your own model.
